about.title: Monterey Park Wrongful Death Claims

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with certain dependents or heirs eligible in other situations. An independent attorney can help clarify where your family fits before any claim moves forward.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, but that window shrinks significantly when a government entity is involved. Waiting to sort out details can quietly cost a family its legal options.

items.title: Losses Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance — not just medical bills. An attorney can help make sure nothing is overlooked in a claim, separate from any related criminal case.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, California law allows two years from the date of death, though claims against a government entity — such as one involving a city-maintained road — have a much shorter deadline. Because Monterey Park corridors like SR-60 involve state and local agencies, it's worth having an attorney review the specifics quickly.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California law gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none of those relationships apply, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing instead. An independent attorney can help sort out exactly where your family stands.

items.question: What if the fatal crash happened on a busy Monterey Park street like Garvey Avenue?
items.answer: High-traffic corridors such as Garvey Avenue, Atlantic Boulevard, and Garfield Avenue see a steady volume of collisions in Monterey Park, and public crash records can become important evidence in a claim. An attorney can help gather and interpret those records as part of building your case.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything for this service?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. We're not a law firm ourselves — we simply help you get connected.
